architecture.mechanism: Adsorption of arsenic using magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles embedded in a porous cellulose matrix.
architecture.intervention: Replace the standard filter media in the rural water filter with pulverized eggshells mixed with magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles contained within a Bemliese teabag or similar porous cellulose sachet.
architecture.expected_effect: Removal of arsenic from groundwater to below 10 μg·L -1 without requiring electricity or liquid chemical dosing, utilizing only the passive flow of water through the nanoparticle-filled bag.
architecture.falsification_test: Pass groundwater with known arsenic concentration >10 μg·L -1 through the modified filter and measure the effluent; if the arsenic concentration remains above 10 μg·L -1, the mechanism is ineffective under these constraints.
